text.p: Swiss shares closed just off the day's highs in relatively high volume trade as foreign buying, a firmer tone in the dollar and higher Wall Street stocks bolstered prices.
"It was a positive surprise today given the impending U.S. elections", a dealer said, adding, "normally, you would not expect such buying interest on a day like this."
Future developments in financial markets was seen depending heavily on the outcome of the elections and particularly on whether Republicans maintain their majority in Congress.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index closed 35.6 points, or 0.95 percent, higher at 3,784.8 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index advanced 17.41 points, or 0.72 percent, to 2,426.59.
Major pharmaceuticals Roche, Ciba and Sandoz all added more than one percent. Roche certificates, which led the actives list, were up 105 francs at 9,750.

U.S. dollar sensitive Surveillance, SMH and Alusuisse, gained ground. Alusuisse, up 22 francs to 963, also profited of news the company's current chief financial officer, Sergio Marchionne, will become chief executive.
Shares of Swiss Re continued their recent strong streak, soaring seven francs to 1,386, a new year's high.
Swiss Bank Corp stood out among banks, gaining 3.50 francs to end at 247.75.
Swissair jumped 34 francs to 1,029 after foreign investors stopped selling the stock, one dealer said.

Utility firm Electrowatt rose six francs to 493. Rumours about CS Holding intending to sell its 45 stake in Electrowatt may have helped the shares, a trader noted. "But we have heard that lots of times lately", he added.
Biotechnology firm Ares-Serono ended nine francs higher at 1,259. The company said nine month group net profit was up 55 percent to 31.94 million francs.
